hints: Focus on Y and Z first, since both are in Period 3 and limited to Groups 13 to 15, so list the only three possibilities.
Notice the chloride clue, only two of those three Period 3 elements give a white solid chloride that hydrolyses to a strongly acidic solution.
Once you have Y, use the melting point order and the rule that first ionisation energy falls down a group to check which X must sit above Y.
walkthrough:
**Narrow down Y and Z to Period 3**

Great start, let's list what we know. Y and Z are both in Period 3 and in Groups 13, 14 or 15.

That gives only three candidates: $\text{Al}$ (Group 13), $\text{Si}$ (Group 14), $\text{P}$ (Group 15).

**Use the white solid chloride clue**

This is the key filter. Both Y and Z form a white solid chloride that gives $\text{pH} < 4$ with water.

$$\text{AlCl}_3(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^- \text{ then hydrolysis gives H}^+$$
$$\text{PCl}_5(s) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$
Both are white solids and give strongly acidic solutions. By contrast, $\text{SiCl}_4$ is a fuming liquid, not a white solid, so Si cannot be Y or Z. Therefore Y and Z must be Al and P in some order.

**Use melting point to fix Y as Al**

We are told melting point of Z is less than melting point of Y.

$\text{Al}$ is a metal with giant metallic bonding, $\text{m.p.} \approx 660^{\circ}\text{C}$. $\text{P}$ is a simple molecular solid, $\text{m.p.} \approx 44^{\circ}\text{C}$ (white) and much lower than Al. So to have $\text{m.p.(Z)} < \text{m.p.(Y)}$, we need $\text{Y} = \text{Al}$ and $\text{Z} = \text{P}$.

**Use ionisation energy to fix X as B**

X is in the same group as Y, so X is also Group 13. First ionisation energy decreases down a group because the outer electron is further away and more shielded.

Since $\text{IE(X)} > \text{IE(Y)}$ and $\text{Y} = \text{Al}$ (Period 3), X must be above Al. That is $\text{B}$ (Period 2). This matches the pair X = B, Y = Al.

options.A: Y = Al fits all clues: Period 3 Group 13, white solid AlCl3 that hydrolyses acidic, and higher melting point than P. X = B is same group, Period 2, so first ionisation energy of B > Al. Perfect match.
options.B: Y = Si fails the chloride test because SiCl4 is a colourless fuming liquid, not a white solid. Also X = Ge is below Si in Group 14, so IE(Ge) < IE(Si), opposite to the required IE(X) > IE(Y).
options.C: Y = P could give white solid PCl5, but then Z would have to be Al and m.p.(Al) > m.p.(P), contradicting m.p.(Z) < m.p.(Y). Also X = As is below P in Group 15, so IE(As) < IE(P), opposite to required.
options.D: X = N above Y = P does satisfy IE(N) > IE(P), which is tempting. But Y = P with Z = Al fails the melting point order, since m.p.(Al) is much greater than m.p.(P), so Z would not be less than Y.
